mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between GDPC1 < -2% YoY and S&P 500 60-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly lower (p > 0.10) when UNRATE > 8% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship (p > 0.05) between INDPRO contraction and S&P 500 60-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between the joint rise of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their 12-month MAs and S&P 500 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 12-month MAs.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the civilian unemployment rate below 5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as firms pass costs to consumers and maintain profit margins.
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation (p > 0.05) between UNRATE < 5% for four months and S&P 500 60-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months signals robust residential investment and consumer confidence, which supports broader economic activity and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when HOUST is above its 12-month MA for eight months.
